newsitem.title: USA: Argosy Iowa riverboat application rejected.
newsitem.headline: Argosy Iowa riverboat application rejected.

text.p: Iowa Racing and Gaming Commission Administrator Jack Ketterer said Wednesday the commission rejected an application by Argosy Gaming Co for a license to operate a riverboat casino near Osceola, Iowa.
Ketterer said the application was rejected by a four to one vote.
Questions raised by commissioners included concerns about Argosy's financial strength and a lack of firm financing for the project, Ketterer said.

G. Dan Marshall, director of investor relations for Alton, Illinois-based Argosy, said commissioners were also concerned about riverboats moving from rivers to lakes. The proposed site would have been the first gambling boat on a lake in the state, he said.
But Marshall also said concerns about the company's financing have been consistently raised when it applies for new licenses.
"The company is pretty highly leveraged right now," Marshall said, noting that Argosy currently has about $350 million in debt.
Argosy has not decided whether it will apply for other licenses in Iowa, Marshall said, noting that desirable river locations in the state are "pretty well saturated."
Argosy also is not officially looking at new cites in other states at this point. The company currently owns or operates five riverboat casinos in the Midwest and Louisiana.
"There hasn't been a statewide (gambling) initiative that has passed since June of 1993," Marshall said of the dearth of new licenses to seek.

The company is currently operating a temporary gaming site in Lawrenceburg, Ind., near the Cincinnati, Ohio, market, that generated $8.9 million in revenues in February with 1,275 gaming sites, no restaraunts, entertainment or parking, Marshall said.
The company hopes to complete the facility, which will include 2,800 to 3,500 gaming sites, by the end of the year, Marshall said.
"The main thing we're working on right now is the brick and mortar in Lawrenceburg," Marshall said.
Argosy shares were down 1/8 at 3-1/2 Wednesday.
